input_signals.name: Cheap Sales Margin Upswing
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), revt), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High sales yield firms should outperform when their post-cost operating margin is improving.
input_signals.reasoning: Sales-to-price can identify low market expectations, but it is most informative when each dollar of revenue is becoming more profitable. The margin trend component separates cheap revenue bases that are improving from cheap firms whose sales remain structurally low quality.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( revt, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( trend( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), xsga ), revt ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Reactivating Asset Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(at, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Asset-cheap firms should outperform when operating profitability on those assets is improving.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts away from static book-to-market crossed with profitability and instead asks whether a low market value for the asset base is being revalidated by rising asset productivity. The profitability leg strengthens the value leg by distinguishing recovering cheap capacity from structurally impaired assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( at, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( trend( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: After-Interest Claim Yield
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(oibdp, xint), ADD(ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dltt), dlc))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when after-interest operating surplus is high relative to the market value of equity plus debt claims.
input_signals.reasoning: The denominator avoids the negative-enterprise-value sign flip by not subtracting cash from total claims. Profitability strengthens cheapness through the numerator: only operating profits remaining after interest expense count as value available to investors.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( oibdp, xint ), add( add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), dltt ), dlc ) )

input_signals.name: Scalable Sales Claim Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, ADD(ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dltt), dlc))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), ADD(cogs, xsga))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with cheap revenue relative to total claims should outperform when that revenue has strong gross surplus relative to operating costs.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the binary profitability gate with a continuous cost-scalability measure, avoiding mass ties and unstable short-leg construction. The interaction targets cheap sales that can plausibly translate into earnings, rather than cheap sales from low-margin or cost-burdened firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( revt, add( add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), dltt ), dlc ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), add( cogs, xsga ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RnD-Adjusted Revenue Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), sale)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap sales should outperform when current operating profitability remains strong even after recognizing that R&D is expensed investment.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding back unreported-or-expensed R&D treats innovative spending as potentially productive rather than purely as a current-period cost. The interaction looks for firms whose revenue is priced cheaply while their operating model, including intangible investment effort, remains economically profitable.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sale, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), sale ) ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation-Backed Capital Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dp, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, dp), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high depreciation capacity relative to market value should outperform when that asset base still earns positive post-depreciation operating returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Depreciation-to-price identifies asset-heavy firms whose installed capital is valued cheaply, but that cheapness can reflect obsolete or unproductive assets. Requiring smoothed operating profit after depreciation helps distinguish underpriced productive capital from melting capital.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( dp, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( ma( ratio( sub( oibdp, dp ), at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Productive SGA Platform Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(xsga, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with underpriced selling and administrative platforms should outperform when gross-profit productivity of that platform is improving.
input_signals.reasoning: SG&A can be wasteful overhead, but it can also represent customer relationships, distribution capacity, and organizational capital. The signal treats SG&A-to-price as cheap intangible capacity only when gross surplus generated per unit of SG&A is trending upward.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( xsga, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( trend( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), xsga ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquid Distribution Capacity
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(che, COALESCE(dvc, 0)), MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, COALESCE(dvc, 0)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high distributable liquidity relative to market value should outperform when operations replenish cash after dividends.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids a pure dividend-yield rank that collapses non-payers into a tied mass by combining dividends with cash balances, while treating missing dividends as economically zero. The profitability leg requires operating surplus after distributions, so cheap liquidity is favored only when it is not being consumed by weak operations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( che, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ), mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( oibdp, coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Overhead-Leverage Cost Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(cogs, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(xsga, revt), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with cheap production throughput should outperform when overhead intensity is falling.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the canonical asset-to-market plus gross-margin stability setup with an operating-leverage mechanism. A high cost-of-goods base relative to market value signals low expectations for the production footprint, while declining SG&A intensity indicates that incremental revenue can convert more effectively into profit.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( cogs, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( neg( trend( ratio( xsga, revt ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Interest-Burden Compression Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(xint, SUB(revt, cogs)), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High gross-profit yield should be most predictive when interest burden relative to gross profit is declining.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the expensive-junk short-side mirror and instead tests whether cheap gross profitability is becoming more available to equity holders. Falling interest burden strengthens the value signal because more of the gross surplus can flow through to residual claimants rather than creditors.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( neg( trend( ratio( xint, sub( revt, cogs ) ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Runway Glamour Burn
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), ADD(che, dlc))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, xint), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when priced richly relative to near-term liquidity while after-interest operating profitability is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: This targets a cash-runway failure mode rather than the generic expensive-junk trade: valuation is high compared with cash and short-term debt capacity, while operations are not producing residual surplus. The signal should be most negative for firms whose market expectations require external financing or rapid profitability recovery.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), add( che, dlc ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( oibdp, xint ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquid Platform Productivity Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(che, xsga), MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(RATIO(oibdp, ADD(cogs, xsga))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with underpriced liquid and organizational resources should outperform when their operating cost base converts efficiently into operating profit.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a cash-to-market recombination of prior liquidity signals; it treats cash plus SG&A as a flexible operating platform whose market price may be too low. The profitability leg requires that the platform is productive, filtering out firms where cash and overhead simply support an inefficient business.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( che, xsga ), mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( oibdp, add( cogs, xsga ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Short-Debt Coverage Liquidity Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, xint), ADD(at, dlc))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Liquid firms should outperform when near-term debt risk is low and after-interest operating profitability is strong.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the noisy interest-to-gross-profit change term and instead measures liquidity relative to market value plus current debt obligations. Profitability strengthens the liquidity value signal by showing that the cash cushion is backed by ongoing operating surplus rather than being a temporary buffer against distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( che, add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), dlc ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( oibdp, xint ), add( at, dlc ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation-Hurdle Sales Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), sale)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap sales should outperform when gross profitability remains strong even after charging current R&D as an innovation hurdle.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids ranking R&D-to-market directly, so non-R&D firms are not collapsed into a zero-valued value leg. Treating missing R&D as zero is economically natural here because it adjusts the margin, rather than using R&D itself as the priced asset.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sale, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), sale ) ) )

input_signals.name: Overhead-Disciplined Gross Yield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), ADD(ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dltt), dlc))), RANK(NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(xsga, revt)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High gross-profit yield should be more predictive when firms maintain low SG&A intensity relative to industry peers.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the prior SG&A-to-price platform leg with gross surplus cheapness relative to total capital claims, avoiding a direct retest of the same value proxy. The profitability interaction asks whether gross profit is likely to reach operating income rather than being absorbed by excessive overhead.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), add( add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), dltt ), dlc ) ) ), rank( neg( ind_adj( ratio( xsga, revt ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net Current Liquidity Surplus
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dltt))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, xint), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with excess cash after current debt should outperform when after-interest operating profitability is strong.
input_signals.reasoning: This distinguishes near-term liquidity surplus from broad net-cash value by treating short-term debt as the key claim against cash while scaling valuation by equity plus long-term debt. Profitability strengthens the signal by showing that the current liquidity surplus is not a temporary buffer for an unprofitable firm.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( che, dlc ), add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), dltt ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( oibdp, xint ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Funding Cash Stock Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(che, oancf), MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(RATIO(oibdp, ADD(cogs, xsga))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with cheap cash plus operating cash generation should outperform when their cost base converts efficiently into operating profit.
input_signals.reasoning: Cash balances are most valuable when replenished by operations, while operating cash flow is more credible when backed by operating profit productivity rather than one-off working-capital movements. The interaction targets self-funding firms whose liquid resources and current cash generation are underpriced by the market.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( che, oancf ), mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( oibdp, add( cogs, xsga ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquidation-Floor Operating Return
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, che), MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(RATIO(oiadp, SUB(at, che))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to book equity plus cash should outperform when their non-cash operating asset base earns strong operating returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the prior short-debt liquidity-leg reuse with a liquidation-floor valuation concept: cash and book equity provide downside support only if the operating assets are not impaired. Scaling operating income by assets net of cash tests whether the market is undervaluing a productive operating business rather than merely rewarding balance-sheet liquidity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( ceq, che ), mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( oiadp, sub( at, che ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Platform Glamour Fade
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), ADD(xsga, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(oibdp, sale))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when the market prices their intangible operating platform richly despite weak operating margins.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the cash-versus-short-debt runway construction and targets a different failure mode: expensive expectations attached to SG&A and R&D-based platforms that are not currently profitable. Treating missing R&D as zero is economically justified because the denominator is total reported intangible operating spend, with SG&A preserving broad coverage and avoiding a pure zero-R&D rank pileup.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), add( xsga, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( oibdp, sale ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RnD-Hurdle Liquidity Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oibdp, xint), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms should outperform when operations remain profitable after both interest expense and R&D investment.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests whether liquid value is strongest when the firm can fund creditors and innovation without eroding the balance sheet. Treating missing R&D as zero is economically justified because the adjustment is an operating-profit hurdle rather than a direct R&D-to-price anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( che, add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), add( dltt, dlc ) ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sub( oibdp, xint ), coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Accumulating Operating Yield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), RANK(TREND(RATIO(che, at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high operating-profit yield should outperform when profitability is being converted into a growing cash buffer.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids reusing the archived operating-productivity leg and instead tests a temporal validation mechanism: cheap operating profits are more credible when cash-to-assets is rising. The cash accumulation condition helps separate underpriced profitable firms from firms whose accounting profitability is not strengthening the balance sheet.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ) ) ), rank( trend( ratio( che, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conservative Core Pretax Yield
input_signals.expression: RATIO(MIN(pi, oiadp), ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))
input_signals.hypothesis: Pretax earnings should be valued more favorably when they are no greater than operating income after depreciation, indicating core operating support.
input_signals.reasoning: This fixes the prior construction flaw by removing the denominator that rewarded near-zero pretax income. Using the lower of pretax income and operating income makes the yield conservative: non-operating windfalls do not inflate the signal, and cheapness is recognized only when earnings are backed by core operations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( min( pi, oiadp ), add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), dlc ) )

input_signals.name: RnD Margin Fade Overprice
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), sale)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), sale), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when sales are priced richly while R&D-adjusted operating margins are deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the prior platform-denominator overpricing signal and instead targets a valuation-expectations failure in revenue multiples. Treating missing R&D as zero is used only as a margin hurdle, while the trend component focuses on worsening economics rather than a static expensive-junk level screen.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), sale ) ), rank( neg( trend( ratio( sub( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), sale ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))), RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(at, dlc))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating-income yield should be more predictive when supported by a strong cash cushion against assets and current debt.
input_signals.reasoning: Post-depreciation operating income yield can be a value trap if the firm lacks balance-sheet flexibility. Conditioning it on cash relative to operating scale and short-term claims favors cheap operating earners that are less exposed to liquidity stress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oiadp, add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), dlc ) ) ), rank( ratio( che, add( at, dlc ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Core-Consistency Operating Yield
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(oiadp, ABS(SUB(pi, oiadp))), ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating-income yield should be more predictive when operating income and pretax income are consistent, indicating that cheap earnings are core rather than non-operating.
input_signals.reasoning: This fixes the prior pretax construction by penalizing large gaps between operating and pretax income instead of rewarding near-zero pretax denominators. The signal is high only when post-depreciation operating profitability is cheap and not contradicted by below-the-line income effects.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( oiadp, abs( sub( pi, oiadp ) ) ), add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), dlc ) )

input_signals.name: Rising Interest Cost Profit Trap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(xint, 1), ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), che))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(oiadp, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when interest expense is rising relative to market value plus cash and post-depreciation operating profitability is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts away from static leverage-stock measures that behaved like generic distress screens and instead focuses on realized financing-cost deterioration. Weak operating returns make rising interest expense harder to absorb, creating a more direct profitability-conditioned value-trap mechanism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( delta( xint, 1 ), add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), che ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( oiadp, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Deleveraging Residual Claim Yield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, xint), ADD(ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dltt), dlc))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: After-interest operating yield should work better when firms are reducing debt rather than relying on leverage to appear cheap.
input_signals.reasoning: Prior after-interest yield had a strong cross-sectional slope but weak alpha, consistent with cheap levered firms contaminating the portfolio leg. Requiring debt reduction tests whether the residual operating surplus is actively de-risking the capital structure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( oibdp, xint ), add( add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), dltt ), dlc ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Core Margin Floor Operating Yield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, xint), sale), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap post-depreciation operating income should outperform when recent after-interest operating margins have remained resilient.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the cosmetic R&D subtraction with a profitability-floor mechanism that applies across the full operating universe, not only R&D reporters. The value leg is strengthened only when the firm has maintained residual operating margin after financing costs, reducing exposure to cheap firms whose operating income is about to deteriorate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oiadp, add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), dlc ) ) ), rank( ts_min( ratio( sub( oibdp, xint ), sale ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profit-Funded Equity Payout Yield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, DELTA(ceq, 1)), ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, xint), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high implied equity payout relative to capital claims should outperform when distributions are supported by after-interest operating profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: This addresses the book-accretion critique by isolating the opposite side of equity growth: earnings not retained in book equity, a proxy for net payout or repurchase activity rather than issuance. The profitability condition helps distinguish shareholder distributions funded by operations from book shrinkage caused by distress or accounting losses.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, delta( ceq, 1 ) ), add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), dlc ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( oibdp, xint ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Asset-Light Operating Expansion Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))), RANK(SUB(GROWTH(revt, 1), GROWTH(at, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap operating-profit yield should be most valuable when revenue is growing faster than the asset base.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids a near-standard retained-earnings yield and instead tests whether cheap operating profitability is being generated with capital efficiency. Firms that expand sales without proportional asset growth are less likely to be value traps requiring heavy reinvestment to sustain profits.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, add( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), dlc ) ) ), rank( sub( growth( revt, 1 ), growth( at, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cost-Inflation Sales Glamour
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), sale)), RANK(SUB(GROWTH(ADD(cogs, xsga), 1), GROWTH(revt, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when priced richly relative to sales while operating costs are growing faster than revenue.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the interest-shock recombination with an operating-leverage deterioration mechanism. A high sales multiple is hardest to justify when cost growth outpaces revenue growth, indicating that market expectations are rising as profitability economics worsen.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( mul( abs( prcc_f ), csho ), sale ) ), rank( sub( growth( add( cogs, xsga ), 1 ), growth( revt, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross-Covered Operating Yield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), ADD(xsga, xint))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap post-depreciation operating income should outperform when gross profit comfortably covers overhead and interest burden.
input_signals.reasoning: Operating-income yield can be temporarily high even when the underlying cost structure is fragile. Gross-surplus coverage of SG&A and interest tests whether the cheap operating income is backed by a sustainable economic spread.
input_signals.author: proposer

input_signals.name: Tax-Converted Pretax Yield
